insights.title: Three securities class actions span 2023-2025
insights.summary: Two Section 10(b)/20(a) class actions in N.D. Cal. (Hayes, and the Pension Fund Action) name the CEO and, in one case, the chief products officer. Together they cover purchasers from Feb 7, 2023 to Oct 22, 2024. A third action, Tripathi v. Enphase, was filed February 17, 2026 against the company, CEO and CFO for purchasers between April 22, 2025 and October 28, 2025. Motion-to-dismiss rulings are pending in all three.
insights.uw_relevance: These are active securities claims against the company and named senior officers. The alleged misstatement periods are not overlapping and run continuously from early 2023 to late 2025.

insights.title: Revenue down about 20% year over year
insights.summary: Revenue was $292M in FY2026 Q2, down 19.6% YoY, after $283M in FY2026 Q1, down 20.6% YoY. FY2026 Q1 posted an operating loss of $30M and a net loss of $7M. In Q2, IQ Battery MWh shipped fell 40%. US revenue fell $44.4M (16%), attributed to the Section 25D credit expiration, and international revenue fell 29%.
insights.uw_relevance: A sustained, policy-driven revenue decline puts pressure on operating results and on the company's forward-looking disclosures. Declines of this kind often feature in disclosure-based securities claims.

insights.title: Q2 profit aided by one-time tariff refunds
insights.summary: After IEEPA tariffs were invalidated, the company received refunds and interest of about $41.0M in Q2 2026 and $11.0M in July 2026. Of these, $45.4M was recorded as a reduction to Q2 cost of revenues, which supported Q2 operating income of $52M. New Section 301 tariffs of 10% to 12.5% were announced July 23, 2026, and LFP battery cells remain sole-sourced from two vendors in China.
insights.uw_relevance: Reported Q2 2026 profitability includes a non-recurring benefit, so earnings quality and disclosure of the refund's effect matter. Tariff changes and China-concentrated cell sourcing are ongoing margin and supply risks.

insights.title: Operating and free cash flow sharply lower

insights.uw_relevance: Much lower internal cash generation leaves less room to absorb litigation costs, tariff shocks or further demand weakness.

insights.uw_relevance: Counterparty stress in the sales channel can cause further write-offs, earnings volatility and questions about the adequacy of credit-loss reserves.

followups.question: Which insider stock sales are cited in the Collins derivative complaint, were they made under Rule 10b5-1 plans, and what pre-clearance and blackout controls apply to directors and executives?
followups.summary: Collins v. Kothandaraman, filed April 23, 2026 in the Delaware Court of Chancery, names non-employee directors and certain executives. It alleges fiduciary breaches tied to the statements challenged in all three class actions and to purported stock sales. Two federal derivative actions remain stayed.
followups.uw_relevance: Insider-sale allegations against individual directors and officers are a core personal D&O exposure, and they are now pending in both Delaware Chancery and federal court.

followups.question: How was the $45.4M IEEPA tariff refund benefit presented in the Q2 2026 earnings release and on the earnings call, and was Q2 operating income also given excluding the refund?
followups.summary: After IEEPA tariffs were invalidated, the company received about $41.0M in refunds and interest in Q2 2026 and $11.0M in July 2026. Of these, $45.4M was recorded as a reduction to Q2 cost of revenues, which supported Q2 operating income of $52M on revenue of $292M.
followups.uw_relevance: If a non-recurring benefit is not clearly separated from underlying results, it can create misstatement exposure while three securities class actions are already pending.

followups.question: How has guidance been updated for the impact of the Section 25D credit expiration and the 40% drop in IQ Battery MWh shipped, and what process does management use to vet forward-looking demand statements?
followups.summary: Revenue was $292M in FY2026 Q2, down 19.6% YoY, after $283M in FY2026 Q1, down 20.6% YoY. US revenue fell $44.4M (16%), attributed to the Section 25D credit expiration, and international revenue fell 29%.
followups.uw_relevance: Sustained, policy-driven revenue declines are a common trigger for disclosure-based securities claims, particularly when guidance proves optimistic.

followups.question: What explains the decline in operating cash flow to $40M in FY2026 Q2 from $103M in Q1, and what operating cash flow level does management expect for the rest of FY2026?
followups.summary: Free cash flow fell from $586M in FY2023 and $480M in FY2024 to $96M in FY2025. In FY2026 it was $83M in Q1 and $26M in Q2, and operating cash flow was $40M in Q2.
followups.uw_relevance: Lower internal cash generation reduces the capacity to fund litigation defense, settlements and tariff shocks without drawing on the balance sheet.

followups.question: How were the $632.5M 0.0% convertible notes due 2026 settled (cash, shares or a mix), and what is the plan for the $575.0M 0.0% notes due 2028, including exposure under the fundamental-change repurchase provisions?
followups.summary: Total debt fell from $1.20B at FY2025 Q4 to $573M at FY2026 Q1, coinciding with the 2026 convertible maturity; the input does not state the settlement mechanics. Debt-to-equity was 0.48x at FY2026 Q2.
followups.uw_relevance: The 2028 notes are the main remaining obligation, and their repurchase provisions could create liquidity demands in a change-of-control or distress scenario.

followups.question: What controls and outside reviews support the company's FEOC and domestic content compliance for its Section 45X AMPTC credits, and what recapture or indemnity obligations does it owe credit buyers?
followups.summary: In March 2026 the company sold $235.0M of 2025 AMPTC at 93% of face value, at a discount of about $16.5M plus about $2.5M in fees. In June 2026 it agreed to sell up to $150.0M of 2026 AMPTC, of which $37.5M of Q1 2026 credits were sold for about $34.9M.
followups.uw_relevance: Credit sales are a material liquidity source, and compliance failures under evolving Treasury guidance could lead to buyer claims and disclosure allegations.

followups.question: How concentrated are receivables among financially stressed distributors and installers, and how has the credit-loss allowance been adjusted since the $6.2M write-off in FY2025?
followups.summary: Management states that prolonged solar demand softness has led to reduced liquidity, bankruptcies and closures among distributors and installers. A customer that filed Chapter 11 in 2024 led to a $6.2M receivable write-off in FY2025.
followups.uw_relevance: Reserves that prove inadequate can cause earnings surprises and questions about the accuracy of financial reporting.

followups.question: What board analysis supported the FY2024 repurchases of $391M (3.81x net income) during the litigated class periods, and what conditions would lead the board to resume buybacks?
followups.summary: Share repurchases were $410M in FY2023, $391M in FY2024 and $130M in FY2025. They have been $0 in every quarter from FY2025 Q3 through FY2026 Q2.
followups.uw_relevance: Buybacks executed while the share price was allegedly inflated can support damages theories and derivative claims against directors.

followups.question: What contingency plans exist if either of the two China-based LFP battery cell vendors is disrupted, and what margin impact does management expect from the Section 301 tariffs announced July 23, 2026?
followups.summary: LFP battery cells remain sole-sourced from two vendors in China. New Section 301 tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on 60 trading partners were announced July 23, 2026.
followups.uw_relevance: Supply disruption or tariff-driven margin compression that was not adequately disclosed in advance can lead to securities claims.

followups.question: Who is the director appointed effective June 11, 2026, what committee roles do they hold, and are they independent of the directors named in the pending derivative suits?
followups.summary: An 8-K Item 5.02 reports that the Board increased its size to eight directors and appointed a new director on the recommendation of the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. The excerpt does not name the appointee or describe committee roles.
followups.uw_relevance: An independent director without litigation conflicts can strengthen oversight of litigation and special committee decisions while derivative suits name non-employee directors.

followups.question: What share reserve increases did the 2021 Equity Incentive Plan amendments approved on May 14, 2025 and May 13, 2026 provide, and how are executive equity grants tied to performance?
followups.summary: Stockholders approved amendments and restatements of the 2021 Equity Incentive Plan at consecutive annual meetings in 2025 and 2026. The 10-K notes the company relies on stock-based awards to retain executives.
followups.uw_relevance: Equity compensation practices bear on the insider-sale allegations in the Collins derivative action and on potential shareholder challenges to compensation.

followups.question: What minimum liquidity level does the board target, and how is the $529M cash balance and $1.39B of working capital allocated between operations, litigation reserves and the 2028 notes?
followups.summary: Cash and equivalents were $529M at FY2026 Q2, the current ratio was 3.45x, working capital was $1.39B and stockholders' equity was $1.18B.
followups.uw_relevance: A strong liquidity cushion lowers the risk of insolvency-related claims against directors and officers while revenue declines.

metric_relevance.buyback_intensity: Buybacks equaled 3.81x net income in FY2024 and 3.36x in FY2025 Q1, compared with 0.75x for full-year FY2025 and 0.00x since FY2025 Q3. Repurchases well above earnings, ahead of a revenue decline, are a likely focus of board-oversight scrutiny in the derivative litigation.
metric_relevance.buybacks: Repurchases were $410M in FY2023 and $391M in FY2024, overlapping the Hayes and Pension Fund class periods, and have been $0 in every quarter from FY2025 Q3 through FY2026 Q2. Large buybacks during periods of allegedly misleading statements, alongside derivative claims over purported insider stock sales, can support claims against directors.
metric_relevance.capex: Capex is modest at $14M in FY2026 Q2 and $41M in FY2025, versus $110M in FY2023. Free cash flow therefore tracks operating cash flow closely, and capex itself is not a significant D&O driver.
metric_relevance.cash: Cash rose to $529M at FY2026 Q2 from $474M at FY2025 year-end even after the 2026 convertible notes were cleared. The balance is partly supported by selling manufacturing tax credits at 93% of face value, including $235.0M of 2025 AMPTC in March 2026. That reliance on credit sales is relevant to defense-cost capacity and to any recapture exposure.
metric_relevance.current_assets: Current assets dropped from $2.61B at FY2025 Q4 to $1.83B at FY2026 Q1, coinciding with the clearing of the $632.5M 2026 convertible notes. They recovered to $1.95B at FY2026 Q2. How the notes were settled explains much of this movement.
metric_relevance.current_liabilities: Current liabilities fell from $1.26B at FY2025 Q4 to $482M at FY2026 Q1 as the 2026 convertible notes came off the balance sheet, and were $565M at FY2026 Q2. The near-term maturity overhang is gone, which reduces refinancing-driven disclosure pressure.
metric_relevance.current_ratio: The current ratio recovered to 3.80x at FY2026 Q1 and 3.45x at FY2026 Q2, from about 1.90x to 2.07x through FY2025 while the 2026 notes were classified as current. Short-term liquidity currently supports funding operations alongside pending litigation.
metric_relevance.debt_to_equity: Debt-to-equity improved to 0.48x at FY2026 Q2 from 1.11x at FY2025 year-end and 1.56x at FY2024, as debt halved and equity grew. Leverage is not currently a primary source of D&O stress.
metric_relevance.ebitda_computed: Computed EBITDA was negative $9M in FY2026 Q1 and $72M in FY2026 Q2, with Q2 lifted by the tariff refund credited to cost of revenues. FY2025 EBITDA of $238M compares with $520M in FY2023, showing how far earnings have fallen since the litigated 2023-2024 period.
metric_relevance.equity: Stockholders' equity rose to $1.18B at FY2026 Q2 from $811M at FY2025 Q1, helped by the halt in buybacks since FY2025 Q3. The rebuild follows heavy FY2023-FY2024 repurchases made during the litigated class periods.
metric_relevance.free_cash_flow: Free cash flow fell from $586M in FY2023 and $480M in FY2024 to $96M in FY2025, then $83M in FY2026 Q1 and $26M in FY2026 Q2. The collapse narrows the cushion for defense costs and capital returns, and contrasts with the cash spent on buybacks in FY2023-FY2024.
metric_relevance.interest_coverage: Coverage was 157.55x in FY2026 Q2 but N/M in FY2026 Q1 because of the operating loss. The Q2 figure is inflated by the tariff refund benefit and the near-zero interest on 0.0% notes, so coverage says little about operating strength here.
metric_relevance.interest_expense: Interest expense is minimal, at $327,000 in FY2026 Q2 and $5M in FY2025, versus $45M in FY2021, because the outstanding convertibles carry a 0.0% coupon. Debt-related risk sits in principal repayment and conversion terms rather than cash interest.
metric_relevance.long_term_debt: Long-term debt of $573M at FY2026 Q2 is the 2028 convertible notes. The earlier drop from $1.20B at FY2024 Q4 to $571M at FY2025 Q1 reflected the 2026 notes moving to current. The 2028 maturity becomes the next capital-structure disclosure point if revenue stays weak.
metric_relevance.net_income: The company posted a $7M net loss in FY2026 Q1 and $36M of net income in FY2026 Q2. The Q2 figure benefited from $45.4M of IEEPA tariff refunds recorded against cost of revenues, so how the one-time benefit was presented matters for disclosure risk. FY2025 net income of $172M remains far below FY2023's $439M.
metric_relevance.operating_cash_flow: Operating cash flow fell from $697M in FY2023 to $137M in FY2025. It was $103M in FY2026 Q1, a quarter that coincided with the $235.0M AMPTC sale, and only $40M in FY2026 Q2. Weaker internal cash generation increases reliance on tax credit monetization to fund litigation and the 2028 notes.
metric_relevance.operating_income: Operating income swung from a $30M loss in FY2026 Q1 to $52M in FY2026 Q2. The Q2 result was supported by $45.4M of one-time tariff refunds booked as a reduction to cost of revenues, so the underlying operating trend is weaker than the headline. New Section 301 tariffs of 10% to 12.5% announced July 23, 2026 are a further margin risk.
metric_relevance.revenue: Quarterly revenue fell from $410M in FY2025 Q3 to $283M in FY2026 Q1 and $292M in FY2026 Q2, and annual revenue is well below the FY2023 peak of $2.29B ($1.47B in FY2025). Management attributes the decline to the Section 25D credit expiration and a 40% drop in IQ Battery MWh shipped. The slide follows the Tripathi class period (April 22 to October 28, 2025), so prior demand statements are likely to be tested against these results.
metric_relevance.revenue_growth_qoq: Sequential revenue fell 16.4% in FY2025 Q4 and 17.6% in FY2026 Q1, after +13.0% in FY2025 Q3, then recovered only 3.2% in FY2026 Q2. The sharp turn right after the Tripathi class period ended on October 28, 2025 is the kind of reversal plaintiffs point to when challenging earlier guidance.
metric_relevance.revenue_growth_yoy: Revenue was down 20.6% YoY in FY2026 Q1 and 19.6% in FY2026 Q2, a second contraction after the 41.9% drop in FY2024 that overlapped the Pension Fund Action class period. Repeated demand-driven declines keep forward-looking statements and guidance under litigation scrutiny.
metric_relevance.total_debt: Total debt fell from $1.20B at FY2025 Q4 to $573M at FY2026 Q1, coinciding with the $632.5M 0.0% convertible notes due 2026. The remaining $575.0M 0.0% notes due 2028 carry fundamental-change repurchase provisions, and the input does not state how the 2026 notes were settled.
metric_relevance.working_capital: Working capital was $1.39B at FY2026 Q2, stable since the 2026 notes were cleared but below $1.91B at FY2023. Channel distress, including the $6.2M receivable write-off in FY2025, is a risk to the quality of receivables within working capital.
